goals: Mechanistic: quantify partitioning of precipitation into surface runoff, ET, and sub-surface recharge/drainage across the Naches basin and attribute it to soil texture and the elevation/climate (rain-snow) gradient
Validation: compare simulated SWE and water-table depth to in-domain observations; check basin water balance against gauges where possible

model_choice.rationale: ELM single-column resolves the full vertical water balance (ET, runoff, drainage/recharge, snow) per (lat,lon); spatial sampling spans basin heterogeneity. Partitioning is a 1-D column question.

answerable: Soil-texture control on runoff/ET/recharge partitioning (SSURGO per-column lever)
Coarse elevation/climate (rain-snow) control on partitioning, via NLDAS-2 orographic precip/temperature gradient across ~1625 m relief
Snow/SWE simulation and SNOTEL peak-SWE comparison (with expected ridgetop underestimation)
Water-table depth comparison at USGS wells, given WTD-informed warm start

not_answerable.aspect: Streamflow/hydrograph reproduction at the 93 USGS gauges
not_answerable.why: Single-column, no lateral transport or routing - no native integrated streamflow

not_answerable.aspect: Sub-12 km elevation control (ridgetop microclimate, within-cell lapse rate)
not_answerable.why: NLDAS-2 is 0.125 deg (~12 km) with no within-cell downscaling

not_answerable.needs: in-domain ET/flux observations or accepted analog-site ET data

sampling_strategy.approach: stratified (elevation bands x dominant soil), with validation columns pinned to observation sites
sampling_strategy.n_justification: 4 elevation bands x 3 dominant soils = 12 cells span the two answerable drivers across the rain-snow transition where partitioning shifts most; light rather than dense because NLDAS gives only ~12 km climate resolution, so finer elevation sampling adds no independent forcing signal.
sampling_strategy.placement_logic: Oversample valley bottoms / riparian corridors (recharge and soil-moisture storage dominate, WTD shallowest) and the mid-elevation rain-snow transition (partitioning most sensitive to snow vs rain). Fewer columns in near-uniform alpine/upper zones.
sampling_strategy.replication: None beyond the strata grid; instead spend budget on pinned validation columns.

sampling_plan.reason: Shallow water table and recharge/storage hotspots; anchors WTD validation and recharge signal (needs warm start).
Partitioning is most sensitive here to snow vs rain; isolates elevation/climate control on ET/runoff/recharge.
Snow-dominated response; spans upper elevation band for the gradient.
Coldest/wettest end-member of the forcing gradient; end-point for partitioning vs elevation.
Pinned to the 6 SNOTEL stations for peak-SWE validation (co-located).
Pinned to USGS well locations for WTD validation and to seed Fan-2013 warm start.

validation_design.comparison: co-located - one column per station; compare annual peak SWE and melt-out timing
validation_design.metric: bias, RMSE, correlation of peak SWE

validation_design.comparison: co-located - requires WTD-informed warm start; note 1-D equilibrium differs from lateral-flow equilibrium (drift is itself a result)
aggregated - basin water-balance sanity check only; NOT a routed hydrograph (no lateral transport). Compare long-term aggregated runoff yield, not timing.
analog - qualitative comparison to regional analog flux sites / literature only; flagged as gap

experiment_summary.primary_treatment: baseline NLDAS-2 forcing, native SSURGO soil, Fan-2013 WTD-informed warm start

requires_capabilities.why: Convert independent column runoff into integrated streamflow
requires_capabilities.blocks: Hydrograph validation against the 93 USGS gauges

requires_capabilities.why: NLDAS-2 12 km cells cannot resolve ridgetop microclimate / within-cell lapse
requires_capabilities.blocks: Fine-scale elevation control; ridgetop SWE accuracy

requires_capabilities.why: Cold-start pins water table at ~8.8 m and recharge ~0
Stratify by elevation band within HUC 17030002

requires_capabilities.capability: SNOTEL and USGS well observation ingest
requires_capabilities.why: Pin validation columns and compute metrics

assumptions: Naches is within CONUS so NLDAS-2 forcing (elevation-resolved to ~12 km) applies.
SSURGO dominant soil textures are resolvable at chosen columns downstream.
USGS wells fall within or near the basin and provide usable WTD for warm start and validation.
Peak-SWE underestimation at high-elevation SNOTEL is expected and interpreted, not treated as model failure.
Forcing period will be a multi-year window within 1980-2018 with adequate spin-up; exact years set downstream.
open_questions: How many USGS wells have usable WTD records inside the basin (sets validation column count)?
Which stream gauges have long-enough daily records for even an aggregated water-balance check?
Preferred analysis period / representative water years, and any drought vs wet-year contrast desired?
Is any regional analog ET/flux dataset acceptable given no in-domain towers?
